epics.title: Move between working locations
epics.value: As a user, I want to move between working locations with little navigation effort so that I can keep my attention on the files I need.
epics.boundary: Adds orientation, location recall, and readable panels. File changes belong to E02.

epics.title: Organize files across locations
epics.value: As a user, I want to organize files across locations so that I can keep useful files in the right place with control over changes.
epics.boundary: Adds selection, file changes, and operation decisions to navigation. Archive packaging belongs to E05.

epics.title: Find files and text in a directory tree
epics.value: As a user, I want to find files and text in a directory tree so that I can act on relevant results without knowing their exact locations.
epics.boundary: Adds discovery across directories. Jumping within the current list belongs to E01; reading a known file belongs to E04.

epics.title: Understand file contents
epics.value: As a user, I want to inspect file contents so that I can understand a file before choosing another tool or changing it.
epics.boundary: Adds read-only inspection of known files, including text, binary data, and images.

epics.title: Work with packaged files
epics.value: As a user, I want to inspect, unpack, and package files so that I can work with content delivered as archives.
epics.boundary: Adds archive navigation, extraction, and ZIP creation. General transfer decisions belong to E02.

epics.title: Use other tools from the current location
epics.value: As a user, I want to use Windows programs and commands from my current file context so that I can continue work in the right tool.
epics.boundary: Adds external launch, command entry, path export, and Windows shell actions.

epics.title: Work with repository changes
epics.value: As a user, I want to inspect repository changes and history and start a commit from Xcmd so that I can understand and finish repository work.
epics.boundary: Adds Git status, history, snapshots, reports, diffs, and a commit handoff to Claude Code.

epics.title: Continue work across application sessions
epics.value: As a user, I want to continue file work across application sessions so that closing the application does not force me to rebuild my workspace.
epics.boundary: Adds saved workspace state. Moving to a new local build belongs to E09.

epics.title: Improve Xcmd while using it
epics.value: As a user-developer, I want to report problems and try new local builds while using Xcmd so that development stays connected to real work.
epics.boundary: Adds feedback on interface elements, syntax reports, release handoff, and a stable launcher for changing releases.

epics.title: Implement workflows over reusable boundaries
epics.value: As a developer, I want to implement workflows over explicit domain and platform boundaries so that new stories can reuse file, search, repository, and presentation services.
epics.boundary: Adds technical capabilities and contracts. An adapter belongs here even when one user story is its only current consumer.

epics.title: Deliver and maintain a reliable application
epics.value: As a developer, I want to package, start, diagnose, and maintain Xcmd consistently so that new workflows can reach the running application safely.
epics.boundary: Adds build inputs, startup, saved state, releases, feedback identities, and the feedback work queue.

stories.title: Navigate two panels without losing the current item
stories.want: move through two directory panels with the keyboard or mouse
stories.why: I can keep source and destination locations in view
stories.behavior: Enter or a double-click opens the current item. Backspace and Ctrl+PageUp open the parent and select the folder just left. Ctrl+` opens the home folder and Ctrl+\ opens the drive root. Tab switches the active panel; a top strip marks it. A missing directory recovers to the nearest existing parent.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to move through two directory panels with the keyboard or mouse so that I can keep source and destination locations in view.

locations.note: Directory, cursor, history, and latest-load state
Cursor choice when returning to a parent
Open the item under the pointer
Current item and active cursor presentation

stories.title: Open a location in the other panel
stories.want: show the current folder or the selected folder in the other panel
stories.why: I can prepare a destination while my source stays active
stories.behavior: Ctrl+Left and Ctrl+Right load the selected folder, or the current folder when a file is selected, into that panel. A selected archive opens its contents there. In a search-result panel the shortcut shows the file's folder with the file selected. Focus stays in the source panel.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to show the current folder or the selected folder in the other panel so that I can prepare a destination while my source stays active.

locations.note: Target choice, archive opening, result location, and source focus

stories.title: Sort files in a predictable order
stories.want: sort the current list by name, extension, date, or size
stories.why: I can find and compare entries more easily
stories.behavior: A column header click or Ctrl+F3/F4/F5/F6 selects the sort. Selecting the same sort again reverses the file order. Directories stay first in ascending natural name order. Cursor and marks stay on the same entries. Git logs keep their newest-first order.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to sort the current list by name, extension, date, or size so that I can find and compare entries more easily.

locations.note: Sort with selection and cursor preservation

stories.title: Jump to names with the keyboard layout I use
stories.want: type part of a visible name and cycle matches
stories.why: I can reach an entry without scrolling through the list
stories.behavior: Alt and a letter start name jumping. Matching accepts the letters of every installed keyboard layout, ignores typed letters that match nothing, and highlights the matched text. Up/Down cycle the matches. Cancelling the jump returns plain typing to the command line.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to type part of a visible name and cycle matches so that I can reach an entry without scrolling through the list.

stories.title: Return to recent and frequent locations
stories.want: choose a recent or frequently used directory
stories.why: I can return to work without typing its path again
stories.behavior: Alt+Down opens the chooser with per-panel recent history and shared frequent directories. A directory earns a visit after ten active seconds in it. The score halves every three days. The frequent list shows up to 30 directories: scored directories first, then directories that were only opened briefly or come from panel history, without a score. Roots, archive locations, Git locations, and the current directory are left out.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to choose a recent or frequently used directory so that I can return to work without typing its path again.

locations.note: Ten active seconds earn a visit

stories.title: Keep named favorite directories
stories.want: add, rename, remove, and open favorite locations
stories.why: I can maintain a short list of useful places
stories.behavior: Ctrl+D opens the Favorites list. Favorites are shared between panels, have unique paths, and are saved immediately. Pins come before frequent directories, and a pinned path does not repeat among them.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to add, rename, remove, and open favorite locations so that I can maintain a short list of useful places.

locations.note: Validation, unique paths, and pin operations
Immediate save and visible save errors

stories.title: Find a saved location and understand missing paths
stories.want: search location names and paths and see when a location is missing
stories.why: I can choose a usable destination without guessing
stories.behavior: Typing in the active chooser column selects the first name or path that contains the text, with keyboard-layout alternatives. Up/Down cycle matches. Escape clears the query before it closes the chooser. Missing directories are marked with their nearest existing parent. An opening error stays visible in the chooser.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to search location names and paths and see when a location is missing so that I can choose a usable destination without guessing.

stories.title: Keep a readable panel layout
stories.want: adjust columns and recognize file types by color
stories.why: I can scan the information that matters in the space available
stories.behavior: Columns keep their chosen widths and hide lower-priority fields when space is limited. Reset column widths restores the defaults. Ordered JSON rules color the type column by file name or extension; the first matching rule wins. Ordinary names use the text color, and Git-ignored names use gray. Cached ignore state carries into child folders until a new repository boundary is found. Reload file colors applies edited rules to existing rows. A reload that fails to read, parse, or validate the rules keeps the current colors and shows a message. Windows file icons come from a technical adapter.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to adjust columns and recognize file types by color so that I can scan the information that matters in the space available.

locations.note: Width preferences, migration, and adaptive visibility
Apply color rules without replacing the list
Reload rules and keep the current colors on error

stories.title: See external directory changes without losing my place
stories.want: refresh directory contents while keeping cursor, marks, and edits stable
stories.why: I can work with files also changed by other programs
stories.behavior: Filesystem changes refresh the panel through a guarded UI update that waits during sensitive interactions. Live Git panels refresh at most every three seconds. Ctrl+R reloads the active panel and keeps its selection. A refresh keeps cursor, marks, and valid folder measurements. Search-result panels keep their matched set.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to refresh directory contents while keeping cursor, marks, and edits stable so that I can work with files also changed by other programs.

locations.note: Wait during interactions and route physical/Git refreshes
Refresh only while the captured context is still valid

stories.title: See the shortcuts for the current context
stories.want: read the main shortcuts for the active panel at the bottom of the window
stories.why: I can find the next action without opening a menu
stories.behavior: A hint row lists the main file, comparison, search, and command-line shortcuts. In a Git log it lists snapshot, commit details, refresh, back, return, and panel shortcuts. In a Git snapshot it lists view, changed files, diff, refresh, back, return, and panel shortcuts. The row updates when the active panel or its location changes.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to read the main shortcuts for the active panel at the bottom of the window so that I can find the next action without opening a menu.

stories.title: Mark a batch independently of the cursor
stories.want: mark files and folders while moving the current cursor
stories.why: I can apply one action to a chosen batch
stories.behavior: Marks, range marking, page and boundary navigation, and clearing marks are separate from the current item. Parent rows cannot be marked. The footer shows the number of selected items and their total size. It shows '≥' while a selected folder is not measured and '(incomplete)' when a measurement is incomplete.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to mark files and folders while moving the current cursor so that I can apply one action to a chosen batch.

locations.note: Batch count, size, and incomplete totals

stories.title: Rename an entry in place
stories.want: edit the full name in its row and commit or cancel
stories.why: I can rename without losing list context
stories.behavior: Shift+F6 selects the full name including its extension. Enter commits, Escape cancels, and Tab commits before it switches panels. Validation or I/O errors keep the editor and the draft. Activating the other panel or focusing another row cancels the edit and drops the draft. Archive and Git locations reject renames with a message for their kind.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to edit the full name in its row and commit or cancel so that I can rename without losing list context.

locations.note: Validate, apply, and keep failed drafts
Cancel the edit when another row gets focus
Cancel the edit when the active panel changes
Read-only message for archive and Git locations

stories.title: Create a folder at the current location
stories.want: create a folder after entering one valid name
stories.why: I can prepare a destination without leaving Xcmd
stories.behavior: F7 opens a name dialog. It accepts one valid name of an entry that does not exist yet. Archive, Git, and search-result locations show a message instead. Successful creation refreshes the list and selects the new folder.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to create a folder after entering one valid name so that I can prepare a destination without leaving Xcmd.

locations.note: Create dialog, validation, refresh, and cursor

stories.title: Create a file ready for editing
stories.want: name a new file and open it in the external editor
stories.why: I can begin writing in the current directory
stories.behavior: Shift+F4 requires a regular directory and a new valid name. The editor must be available before the file is created. Creation fails when the file already exists. The new file becomes current and opens in Notepad++.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to name a new file and open it in the external editor so that I can begin writing in the current directory.

locations.note: Delegate new-file preparation to the editor adapter

stories.title: Copy or move a batch to an explicit destination
stories.want: copy or move selected entries with an editable destination
stories.why: I can place files where I intend
stories.behavior: F5/F6 capture the selected entries when the dialog opens and resolve the destination text when it is submitted. A single item can receive a new name; several items require an existing directory. Targets inside the source are rejected. Copying and moving links is rejected and the link stays unchanged. A folder copied onto an existing folder merges into it and keeps destination-only entries. A move removes each source only after its transfer succeeds. Copies keep the creation, modification, and access times, the Hidden, ReadOnly, System, and Archive attributes, and the additional data streams. New copies inherit destination permissions.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to copy or move selected entries with an editable destination so that I can place files where I intend.

locations.note: Writable paths and safe source/target relations
Copy/move target, link, and merge rules
Merge folders and remove moved sources only after success
Capture selections and enqueue the requested transfer
Additional data streams and inherited permissions

stories.title: Duplicate an entry in the same folder
stories.want: copy an entry under another name in the current directory
stories.why: I can make a local variant quickly
stories.behavior: Shift+F5 opens the copy dialog with the current directory as an editable destination. A batch cannot target its own source directory, and a source cannot replace itself.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to copy an entry under another name in the current directory so that I can make a local variant quickly.

stories.title: Transfer files through the Windows clipboard
stories.want: copy or cut a file batch and paste it into the displayed directory
stories.why: I can transfer files between Xcmd and other Windows tools
stories.behavior: Ctrl+C/Ctrl+X write the batch as Windows files; Ctrl+V pastes into the displayed directory. Cut rows are dimmed and the sources stay until paste. Nested sources are reduced to their top folder. A copy into the source folder gets a free '(copy)' name with a number when needed. A cut into the source folder changes nothing. A move removes only the completed sources and keeps skipped or failed ones for another paste. Archive and Git entries and destinations show a message instead.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to copy or cut a file batch and paste it into the displayed directory so that I can transfer files between Xcmd and other Windows tools.

locations.note: Keep skipped or failed cut items available
Source reduction, free copy names, and paste policy

stories.title: Drag files to another folder or program
stories.want: drag selected entries with the mouse and drop files onto a panel
stories.why: I can move files between Xcmd and other Windows programs by pointing
stories.behavior: Dragging a row with the left or right mouse button starts a Windows drag of the marked group when the row is marked, or of that row alone. A click on a marked row without movement selects only that row; Ctrl+click toggles it. Windows copies, moves, or creates shortcuts at the target. Items dropped on a panel go to the folder row under the pointer, which is highlighted, or to the panel folder. Holding the pointer near the top or bottom edge scrolls the list. Drag and drop works with physical folders; archive, Git, and search-result panels are skipped.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to drag selected entries with the mouse and drop files onto a panel so that I can move files between Xcmd and other Windows programs by pointing.

locations.note: Drag start, selection on release, drop destination, highlight, and edge scrolling
Select or toggle a clicked marked row

stories.title: Choose how to delete a batch
stories.want: confirm recycling or permanent deletion
stories.why: I can control the consequence of removing files
stories.behavior: F8/Delete select the Recycle Bin; Shift+F8/Shift+Delete select permanent deletion. The confirmation lets the user change the mode. Recycling works on local fixed drives. When Windows offers permanent deletion instead of recycling, Xcmd refuses it and keeps the item.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to confirm recycling or permanent deletion so that I can control the consequence of removing files.

locations.note: Execute the selected deletion mode through the operation store
Recycle only on local fixed drives

stories.title: Resolve conflicts without abandoning a transfer
stories.want: skip, rename, or replace a conflicting target
stories.why: I can finish the useful parts of a copy or move
stories.behavior: A conflict prompt appears for a file target, a folder against a file, or a link target. The default decision is Skip. Replace works only for regular files. Apply to all repeats Skip or Replace for matching conflict kinds in the same request. Escape or closing the prompt cancels the operation. Identical files are skipped without a prompt after a content and metadata comparison.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to skip, rename, or replace a conflicting target so that I can finish the useful parts of a copy or move.

locations.note: Wait for a suitable moment before prompting

stories.title: Queue work and understand its progress
stories.want: submit long file operations and inspect progress and results
stories.why: I can keep using the panels while work runs
stories.behavior: Requests run in order with targets captured at submission. Counting comes before execution. The summary shows processed and total files, skipped and failed items, incomplete counts, queued requests, and an estimate of the remaining time. Bytes drive the progress bar. The details view lists the operations of the session and the last 100 outcomes of each operation.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to submit long file operations and inspect progress and results so that I can keep using the panels while work runs.

locations.note: Count work and mark incomplete inventories

stories.title: Recover from errors or stop queued work
stories.want: retry, skip, or cancel work when an item fails
stories.why: I can keep completed work and make the next decision explicitly
stories.behavior: A failed item offers Retry, Skip, Skip similar errors, and Cancel. Identified locks instead show application links, plain executable/PID summaries, and Kill for the listed processes. Kill can lose unsaved changes. The operation retries when all listed processes exit; cancellation stops that wait. Similar errors are grouped by exception type. Counting, current work, and queued work can be cancelled. Completed filesystem changes stay in place. Partial and not-started outcomes stay visible.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to retry, skip, or cancel work when an item fails so that I can keep completed work and make the next decision explicitly.

locations.note: Application links, plain PID summaries, Kill and automatic retry
Present failures without stealing an active edit

stories.title: Measure folder sizes before acting
stories.want: calculate one or all folder sizes in the panel
stories.why: I can judge the amount of data in a selection
stories.behavior: Space measures the current folder. Alt+Shift+Enter measures every child folder in the panel list; pressing it again or Escape cancels. Work runs in the background. Links are skipped and counted separately. Read errors mark a total incomplete. Results for an outdated listing are discarded.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to calculate one or all folder sizes in the panel so that I can judge the amount of data in a selection.

locations.note: Start, cancel, and apply valid measurements
Combine selected file and measured folder totals

stories.title: Find files by name or relative path
stories.want: search below a location using a name fragment, whole name, or mask
stories.why: I can find files whose exact locations I do not know
stories.behavior: Alt+F7 opens the search window for the active location. Contains and Whole name modes compare names; a pattern with * or ? always matches the whole name or relative path. An option treats * and ? as literal characters. Patterns can include relative paths. Folders are returned as name results too. Query length and regex validity are checked before work starts.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to search below a location using a name fragment, whole name, or mask so that I can find files whose exact locations I do not know.

locations.note: Validate and start an explicit query

stories.title: Find text across files
stories.want: search file contents with literal text or a regular expression
stories.why: I can locate information inside a directory tree
stories.behavior: The query supports case and regex options and returns the first match in each file with its line and a snippet of up to 240 characters. Encoding detection tries the detected encoding and then UTF-8, Windows-1251, Windows-1252, and code page 866. Binary files are skipped. Decoding failures, regex timeouts, and regex lines over 256K characters are reported as failures.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to search file contents with literal text or a regular expression so that I can locate information inside a directory tree.

locations.note: Search file text and publish a first match
Publish a unique result within limits

stories.title: Get useful search results before expensive areas
stories.want: search ordinary files first and understand the search scope
stories.why: I can get useful answers before scanning caches and large archives
stories.behavior: The session uses separate small-file, large-file, and archive lanes. Archive roots are read by their own worker while the ordinary traversal runs. Git-tracked paths are kept; ignored or untracked dependency and cache folders are deferred. Nested archives are reported as skipped. File and result limits bound a session.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to search ordinary files first and understand the search scope so that I can get useful answers before scanning caches and large archives.

locations.note: Priority lanes, deferred paths, archives, and limits

stories.title: Inspect skipped areas and search them deliberately
stories.want: see skipped paths and failures and choose further locations to search
stories.why: I can judge whether the result set is sufficient
stories.behavior: The window lists skipped and failed paths with reasons, including the Git rule source when it is known. Search skipped files extends the session. A double-click on a skipped or failed path starts a new search there; that path becomes the search root for later searches and for To panel.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to see skipped paths and failures and choose further locations to search so that I can judge whether the result set is sufficient.

locations.note: Search one chosen location and change the root
Keep deferred paths and report failure categories

stories.title: Control a search without losing useful results
stories.want: stop a search, revise its query, and reuse earlier queries
stories.why: I can explore step by step without unclear background changes
stories.behavior: Results appear progressively. Stop keeps the results and marks the coverage as partial. Edited options take effect when Search is requested. Name and text history and the settings are saved for later sessions. A new request cancels and retires the earlier one.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to stop a search, revise its query, and reuse earlier queries so that I can explore step by step without unclear background changes.

locations.note: Distinguish edited query from running query

stories.title: Go from a search match to the file
stories.want: open the matching file or locate it in a panel
stories.why: I can continue work from the result
stories.behavior: F3 opens a viewer at the text match with the detected encoding. Go to file shows the result in its folder, or in its archive location, in the panel that was active when the search window opened. Go to file closes the search window and focuses that panel.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to open the matching file or locate it in a panel so that I can continue work from the result.

stories.title: Use search results as a working panel
stories.want: send a result snapshot to a panel and act on its entries
stories.why: I can organize files found in different directories
stories.behavior: To panel (Alt+P) sends the results to the panel that was active when the search window opened and closes the window. The result panel shows relative labels and supports marks, sorting, viewing, renaming, and source operations. Ctrl+Left/Right shows a result in its folder in the other panel; for an archive result it opens the archive there. Escape, Backspace, or Ctrl+PageUp restore the earlier panel. Refresh removes unavailable matches. The snapshot is saved with the workspace. Windows group menus need results from one folder.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to send a result snapshot to a panel and act on its entries so that I can organize files found in different directories.

locations.note: Snapshot state, operations, restore, and result refresh

stories.title: Inspect files in independent viewers
stories.want: open one or more viewers and move through the displayed file list
stories.why: I can read files while the panels remain usable
stories.behavior: F3 opens independent non-modal viewers. Previous and next file follow the file list captured when the viewer opened. Captions show the origin of virtual documents and mark read-only documents. Ctrl+W closes a viewer.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to open one or more viewers and move through the displayed file list so that I can read files while the panels remain usable.

locations.note: Capture all file rows and the current file
Origin caption and read-only external-action guard

stories.title: Choose an inspection mode and encoding
stories.want: switch between text, binary, hex, and image inspection
stories.why: I can interpret files that do not fit the first detected mode
stories.behavior: The viewer detects common raster image signatures and the text encoding. Keys 1–4 and the View menu change the mode; the Encoding menu changes the encoding. The page renders again after a change. Image mode is enabled only for files with a supported image signature, and images are decoded with size limits. Ctrl+I shows file information.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to switch between text, binary, hex, and image inspection so that I can interpret files that do not fit the first detected mode.

locations.note: Apply manual encoding and reset search state

stories.title: Read large files with bounded memory
stories.want: scroll and jump through a large file with meaningful position information
stories.why: I can inspect large content with bounded memory
stories.behavior: The viewer reads overlapping bounded pages and maps text positions to byte offsets. The scroll bar and Home/End cover the whole file. Progress shows the visible part of the file. W toggles word wrap and keeps the current byte position. Text selection and copy work on the loaded document window.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to scroll and jump through a large file with meaningful position information so that I can inspect large content with bounded memory.

locations.note: Whole-file scroll, navigation, offsets, and progress
Keep the byte position when toggling wrap

stories.title: Find text throughout a viewed file
stories.want: find literal text and move to the next or previous match
stories.why: I can reach relevant content beyond the visible page
stories.behavior: Ctrl+F or Alt and a letter start a case-insensitive literal search. F3/Tab and Shift+F3/Shift+Tab move through matches and wrap around. Requests are debounced and outdated results are cancelled. The search covers the whole file. Open viewers in one process share the query.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to find literal text and move to the next or previous match so that I can reach relevant content beyond the visible page.

locations.note: Find entry, direction, match selection, and outdated-request guards
Share the current find text between viewers

stories.title: Read source with an appropriate language
stories.want: use automatic or manual syntax highlighting
stories.why: I can understand code structure while inspecting a file
stories.behavior: The language comes from the file extension, from names such as Dockerfile, Makefile, and .editorconfig, or from a python, pwsh, or sh shebang. The Syntax language menu offers plain text and manual choices. Highlighting covers the first 1 MiB of a file, lines up to 8,192 characters, and a time budget of 1.5 seconds in total and 250 ms per line. Outside these limits the text stays readable as plain text. Markdown and CSV show highlighted source text.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to use automatic or manual syntax highlighting so that I can understand code structure while inspecting a file.

locations.note: Language selection, highlighting request, and fallback
Reset language choice when changing files
Language choice by file name and shebang

stories.title: Choose comfortable reading colors
stories.want: choose a viewer theme shared across open viewers
stories.why: I can read different files with consistent colors
stories.behavior: Nine named themes are available. A change updates all open viewers and the saved preference. Selection and search highlights stay while colors change. Token contrast comes from a rendering service.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to choose a viewer theme shared across open viewers so that I can read different files with consistent colors.

locations.note: Apply theme changes to all viewers

stories.title: Follow a changing log file
stories.want: follow the end of a growing file
stories.why: I can observe new output without repeatedly reopening it
stories.behavior: Ctrl+Shift+F toggles Follow end of file. Follow works for regular files and is disabled for images, archive members, archive reports, and read-only documents such as Git snapshots. Polling every 500 ms detects growth, truncation, and changed bytes. Moving up, Home/End, the scroll bar, search, and a mode change pause following.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to follow the end of a growing file so that I can observe new output without repeatedly reopening it.

locations.note: Follow state, polling, and pause conditions

stories.title: Continue from a viewed file in another program
stories.want: open the viewed file with Windows or in the external editor
stories.why: I can act after inspecting its contents
stories.behavior: F4 sends a writable physical file to Notepad++, and Open externally sends it to its Windows association. Read-only documents block both actions. Archive members open externally through a temporary copy; see E05.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to open the viewed file with Windows or in the external editor so that I can act after inspecting its contents.

stories.title: Browse an archive like a location
stories.want: enter supported archives and nested members
stories.why: I can inspect their structure before extracting
stories.behavior: Enter opens common archive extensions; Ctrl+PageDown probes any file, including supported self-extracting containers. Parent navigation and nested archive paths work. Opening can be cancelled with Escape. Archive entries are read-only. Encrypted entries and unsupported content produce errors.
stories.statement: As a user, I want to enter supported archives and nested members so that I can inspect their structure before extracting.

stories.title: Inspect an archive and its members
stories.want: view archive information or open an individual member
stories.why: I can understand packaged content without a full extraction

stories.statement: As a developer, I want to compose the desktop host and dispose its background work predictably so that I can diagnose failures and add services with clear lifetimes.

stories.title: Select and hand off immutable local releases
stories.want: resolve release evidence and confirm a replacement process is ready
stories.why: I can ship builds while the working process stays open until its replacement is ready
stories.behavior: ReleaseFiles validates release IDs, the protocol, and check results with a positive total and zero failures, and reads releases/latest.txt. ReleaseCatalog identifies the running release from the process directory. The handoff uses a readiness handshake with timeouts and cleans up a failed child. The standalone launcher is built from a subset of Infrastructure.
stories.statement: As a developer, I want to resolve release evidence and confirm a replacement process is ready so that I can ship builds while the working process stays open until its replacement is ready.

stories.why: I can change installed builds while the application entry point stays the same
stories.behavior: Windows shortcut and property-store COM adapters keep the app identity and relaunch metadata consistent. The Desktop wrapper reports initialization failures.
